prize_parts.citation: For the conception and first demonstration of targeted protein degradation by PROTACs, bifunctional small molecules that direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to destroy chosen proteins
For the development of base editors that chemically convert one DNA base into another at programmed sites without double-strand breaks

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1: Crews and Deshaies for PROTACs, Liu alone for base editing. Having read the full exchange, I think the round-1 record supports this more than it did before. Six of eight members back B014, but they hold three different third names, which shows that the third seat is a credit judgement and not a scientific one; the founding concept has two names on which every supporter agrees. Base editing meets the test I apply to every candidate: a biological process, DNA repair of a deaminated base, was converted into a defined chemical reaction (cytidine or adenosine deamination in a Cas-bound single-stranded window) that other laboratories reproduced quickly and that biologists now use as a general tool. The adenine editor is the clearest case because it required evolving a deaminase with no natural DNA activity, so the chemistry was invented and not borrowed. Measured editing outcomes, including bystander editing and off-target deamination, were characterised quantitatively and independently, which is what I trust most.
statement.case_against: The two parts sit in one neighbourhood, chemical biology and drug discovery, and the committee may reasonably prefer one part from there plus a part from synthetic or physical chemistry, as Somfai proposes. A PROTAC-only citation omits Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures, Handa and Ito's identification of cereblon, and Sakamoto and Kim from the 2001 paper, so it reads narrower than the field. Neither modality has the clinical proof that would settle maturity: no heterobifunctional degrader is approved, and base editing has only a short patient record and no long-term safety data. For base editing, the 2020 CRISPR prize leaves a fair question about distinctness, and I have still not independently verified the priority between the cytosine base editor and Target-AID papers.

responses.point: Linke argues that induced proximity is one principle in two molecular forms, PROTACs and thalidomide-type glues, so a single citation with Crews, Deshaies and Handa can cover both and gives the prize two pillars.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument for a broad citation, and the chair's first question is fair. I still do not take Handa as the third name, for a reason about what was measured. Cereblon as the thalidomide target explained how an existing drug works, and that explanation later made glues a design strategy. The PROTAC was designed from first principles and shown to work. If the committee wants a principle-level citation, I would accept your wording but only if it names the discovery in the citation, since a broad sentence over a mechanistic finding invites the objection that the two lineages are stitched together. Because I would use the freed seat for Liu, my answer to the chair is that Handa's discovery is real and not implied by Crews and Deshaies, but I weigh it below the design concept and below base editing for the third seat.

responses.point: Sparr backs Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, citing Ciulli's VHL ligands and structural work as making the approach rational, and says base editing has clearer therapeutic outcomes than degraders.
responses.response: On the second point we agree in direction and I would put it more carefully. Base editing has a shorter patient record than you may be assuming, so I treat its clinical outcomes as promising and unsettled, not as the decider. On Ciulli, I accept that the structural work on ternary complexes is what made degrader design rational, and Aqvist's point about cooperativity and free energy supports it. My difficulty is the cost: a third name in B014 removes the single seat that makes a B042 part possible within three people. If the committee prefers B014 alone, then Ciulli is the better third name than Handa for a PROTAC-centred prize, and I would say that openly.

responses.point: Aili asks specifically about priority and credit in the 2001 PROTAC work, since Sakamoto and Kim are co-authors but are in none of the preferred configurations, and names Ciulli as third.
responses.response: The 2001 paper has four authors and I am not comfortable calling Crews and Deshaies the only inventors. My reading of the record, which I cannot check beyond the nominations, is that Crews and Deshaies conceived and led the programme, while Sakamoto and Kim carried out the work as the first-generation experimentalists, which is the same pattern as Komor and Gaudelli with Liu. The three-name limit forces a choice, so I would state in the committee's public reasoning that this is a credit judgement and not a statement that the others did not contribute. I do not think the priority question changes the scientific case, only the names.

responses.point: Somfai pairs Liu's base editing with Buchwald and Hartwig's C-N coupling and omits B014, arguing that Pd amination is a general method that changed how chemists build bonds.
responses.response: We share Liu alone as the base-editing attribution, and your point about the adenine editor's directed evolution is the part I find most convincing. Where I differ is on the pairing. The question is whether C-N coupling adds a new capability beyond the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and the chair's fifth question asks exactly that. Even if it is, B014 has support from six members and has the broadest independent confirmation, so leaving it out strikes me as the larger departure from the committee's own judgement. I keep B057 as an alternative and would move to it if the committee wants a non-biological second part.

responses.point: Zou notes that a few years' wait would carry little cost for PROTACs because clinical proof is still maturing, and that Handa's inclusion makes the prize read as two lineages stitched together.
responses.response: I agree with you that the two-lineage reading is a risk, and it is part of why I keep the citation tied to the designed bifunctional molecule. On timing, I take the point that waiting is cheap, but the same argument would apply to base editing, and I do not want to apply it to one candidate and not the other. Both have independent confirmation across many laboratories of the underlying chemistry, which is the maturity criterion I rely on. Clinical approval would strengthen either case but I do not require it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept two chemical-biology parts in one year, or prefer one such part plus a part from synthetic or physical chemistry.
Whether Ciulli or Handa is the right third name if the committee chooses B014 alone; I rank Ciulli ahead for a PROTAC-centred citation.
How to treat Sakamoto and Kim, and Komor and Gaudelli, within a three-name limit.
Whether priority between the cytosine base editor and Target-AID papers affects Liu's sole credit; I have not verified this independently.
Whether clinical outcomes for degraders or base editors in the next few years should change the timing.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. I work on nucleotide metabolism and DNA repair, which is adjacent to how base editing exploits uracil and inosine repair, but I have no collaboration or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate. I note that Linke, Somfai and Sparr are Lund colleagues, and Brzezinski and Zou are Stockholm colleagues; I have no such tie to any of them beyond the Umeå-based committee work.
